newsitem.title: CHINA: China Central Reserve says no copper sale plans.
newsitem.headline: China Central Reserve says no copper sale plans.

text.p: China has no immediate plan to sell copper on the international market, an official of the Central Reserve Bureau in Shanghai said on Tuesday.
The official said that the Central Reserve had not received any order from the Chinese government to sell copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
The reserve had sold copper on the LME at about this time last year, a second official said, but this year there was no intention to do the same.
The amount sold onto the market in June 1996 totalled about 100,000 tonnes, the official said.
The officials declined to give further details, saying that they acted only on central government orders.
Rumours are swirling on the Shanghai and London markets that the Central Reserve is preparing to sell up to 50,000 tonnes of copper on the LME as prices are currently high.
A local copper trader said senior Central Reserve Bureau officials are currently in Shanghai considering market movements. This could not be immediatley confirmed.
LME copper moved off its recent highs in overnight trading on Monday as a small fall in stocks failed to excite the market.
Last three months business on the kerb was at $2,482 a tonne, down $47 from last Friday.
